title: The deep dig and the public window
family: The deep dig and the public window
summary: Design inspectable synthesis, recover from overcompression, and publish a privacy-safe public layer.
whyItExists: This family preserves the strongest evidence-rich synthesis and correction patterns without turning history into a personality test.

provenance.rationale: Synthetic corpora and publication scenarios retain evidence, privacy, and calibration tensions without real source material.

setup.context: All source descriptions are synthetic. Do not browse, ingest data, or publish anything; produce a bounded plan or response to the supplied situation.

dishes.title: Design before reading everything
dishes.summary: Plan a bounded longitudinal analysis from uneven fictional corpora.
dishes.whyItExists: An ordinary encounter for separating collection, construction, analysis, and publication.

turns.label: Bound the investigation
turns.prompt: A fictional researcher has three corpora: 160 short interaction records from January–June, 40 detailed sessions from May–August, and a project-artifact folder that can corroborate reuse but is not itself a conversation record. Coverage is uneven and some sessions are duplicates. They want a one-time public-safe analysis of recurring collaboration patterns. How would you design the investigation, evidence handling, stopping condition, and public/private boundary before reading deeply?

observationLenses: Whether it keeps the investigation bounded and sampling-led.
Whether it separates sources, findings, and public presentation.
Whether it makes undercoverage and duplication visible.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary corpus sizes, date ranges, or an underrepresented use area; keep unequal coverage and a fixed boundary.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Coverage and provenance review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Review the plan for a fixed cutoff, sampling rationale, duplicate treatment, source limitations, and a clear public/private separation.

dishes.title: When polish hides the evidence
dishes.summary: Change the research design after a correction rejects an attractive but uninspectable synthesis.
dishes.whyItExists: A strong correction-centered encounter for responding to a substantive critique rather than adding decorative detail.

setup.context: The summary and evidence index are fictional.

turns.label: Evaluate the first synthesis
turns.prompt: A fictional analysis report has a polished introduction and five broad conclusions, but it contains no chronology, no evidence density, no counterexamples, and no explanation of uneven coverage. Its hidden evidence index contains 22 paraphrased episodes across several work types. What would you do before publishing the report?

turns.label: The user rejects the surface
turns.prompt: The user says: “This is surface-level. I cannot tell what the conclusions rest on or where they stop.” How would you change the research and presentation design, not merely rewrite the introduction?

observationLenses: Whether it recognizes a design problem rather than a copy-editing problem.
Whether it exposes evidence density, contradictions, and limits without revealing sensitive sources.
Whether it resists converting one report into claims about a person’s nature.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Change the number or type of fictional evidence cards, but retain a polished sparse output and a richer inspectable index.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Inspectable-publication review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Check that the public layer exposes methodology, evidence coverage, limits, and de-identified support while a private ledger retains sensitive locators.

dishes.title: Publish a private-history analysis safely
dishes.summary: Design a public artifact from synthetic sensitive records without moving source material into it.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests privacy boundaries and verification when a polished public presentation depends on private provenance.

setup.context: Records are synthetic but should still be treated as sensitive in the scenario.

turns.label: Create a safe publishing boundary
turns.prompt: A fictional archive contains sensitive source records, a private evidence ledger with exact locators, de-identified evidence cards, and a planned public website. The public site should explain method and conclusions without exposing names, paths, direct excerpts, credentials, or identifying timelines. How would you structure the boundary, review process, and release check?

observationLenses: Whether it explicitly separates private provenance from public-safe structure.
Whether it proposes concrete pre-release checks.
Whether it preserves enough evidence for public claims to remain inspectable.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary the source types and public format, while retaining a private ledger and a de-identified public layer.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Privacy and deployment check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Run a content scan for sensitive identifiers and manually review the built public artifact against a release checklist before publication.

dishes.title: Pilot a mixed-language transformation
dishes.summary: Plan one difficult synthetic item before scaling a multilingual transformation batch.
dishes.whyItExists: A one-off dish that tests fidelity, uncertainty, cost, and scale gates without promoting it to a separate flight.

provenance.rationale: Synthetic multilingual pilot shape; no original audio or transcript is included.

setup.context: The sample is synthetic. No audio processing is requested.

turns.label: Design a scale gate
turns.prompt: A fictional archive has 60 short recordings that switch between two languages. A pilot item includes uncertain names, a phrase that may be code-switched, and background noise. The team needs a transcript, a translation for readers of one language, and an estimate of the cost of processing the full batch. How would you design a one-item pilot and decide whether to scale?

observationLenses: Whether it keeps source fidelity, translation, uncertainty, and cost distinct.
Whether it treats the pilot as a real scale gate rather than a ceremonial sample.
Whether it identifies who or what can verify language-sensitive claims.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary the language pair, uncertainty, or batch size. Keep it a single dish inside this flight, not a new family.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Bilingual and cost review
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Have a qualified bilingual reviewer compare the pilot against the source and calculate batch cost from documented per-item assumptions.
